features.title: Strict skill resolution
features.summary: Every skill name, whether from a resume, a job or a form, is matched to one canonical skill or rejected. Nothing else can become a Skill node.
how: The name is normalized: Unicode cleanup, lowercase, '-', '_' and '/' become spaces.
It must match a canonical skill or one of its aliases exactly ('k8s' → Kubernetes, 'torch' → PyTorch).
There is deliberately no fuzzy matching, so 'Java' can never turn into 'JavaScript'.
Anything unknown is returned as unmapped instead of being invented.

inputs.name: names
inputs.label: Skill names (comma or newline separated)
inputs.default: pytorch, k8s, sklearn, RAG, Pinecone, Java, JavaScript, Rust, Pytorchh

features.title: Skill ontology (60 skills, 107 aliases, 46 prerequisites)
features.summary: The canonical vocabulary lives in a version-controlled JSON file and is served as graph data for the 3D explorer, with no database read needed.
how: ontology/skills.json lists skills, aliases, domains and PREREQUISITE_OF chains.
On load it is validated: unique names, no alias collisions, known prerequisites, no cycles.
The API turns it into nodes and links that react-force-graph-3d draws directly.

features.title: Unmapped-term review queue
features.summary: Skill names that matched nothing are stored as a plain list on the user or job, at zero graph-node cost, and aggregated here for review.
how: During ingestion, unknown terms go into the owner's unmapped_skills list property.
This endpoint unwinds those lists across all users and jobs and counts each term.
Useful terms get added to skills.json, then the seed is regenerated.

features.title: Create a user (no LLM)
features.summary: Creates a User node from a form. The id is generated if empty; a taken id returns 409 instead of overwriting.
how: The target domain is resolved against the 4 canonical domains.
One write transaction checks the id, creates the node and links it to its domain.

features.title: List users
features.summary: Every user with their skill count and how many of their terms were unmapped.
how: A single read query counts HAS_SKILL edges per user, paginated with skip and limit.

features.title: View a user's skills
features.summary: A user's canonical skills with proficiency and where each came from (resume or manual), plus unmapped terms.
how: Reads the User node and its HAS_SKILL edges; returns 404 if the id doesn't exist.

features.title: Set skills by hand (strict)
features.summary: Replaces a user's whole skill list. Aliases resolve to canonical skills; unknown names are kept as unmapped, never as nodes.
how: Each name is resolved; duplicates such as 'torch' and 'PyTorch' collapse to one, keeping the higher proficiency.
One transaction deletes the old HAS_SKILL edges and MERGEs the new ones on the node pair, so duplicates are impossible.
Proficiency must be between 0 and 1, otherwise you get a 422.

features.title: Parse a resume (Gemini, cached)
features.summary: Gemini extracts skills from resume text, which are then resolved strictly and written. Identical text never costs a second Gemini call.
how: The text is hashed. If it matches the user's stored source_hash, the call returns 'unchanged' with no LLM call and no write.
Otherwise the extraction comes from the in-memory cache or, through the rate limiter, from Gemini in JSON mode.
Resume-derived skills are replaced; skills you entered by hand are kept.
Run it twice with the same text to see 'unchanged'.

inputs.name: text
inputs.label: Resume text
inputs.default: Dashboard Tester. ML engineer, 3 years of production Python and PyTorch. Built RAG pipelines with LangChain and Pinecone. Familiar with Docker and SQL.

features.title: Delete a user
features.summary: Removes the user and their edges. Shared Skill and Domain nodes stay.
how: DETACH DELETE in one transaction; returns 204, or 404 if the id doesn't exist.

features.title: Create a job from structured fields (no LLM)
features.summary: Creates a job with core, preferred and nice-to-have skills. A skill listed in two tiers keeps the higher tier.
how: Skills are resolved strictly and deduplicated with precedence core > preferred > nice_to_have.
One transaction writes the posting and its REQUIRES_SKILL and IN_DOMAIN edges; a taken id returns 409.

features.title: Create a job from description text (Gemini)
features.summary: Gemini parses a job description into tiers and skills, then the same strict pipeline writes it.
how: A taken id is rejected before the LLM call, so a conflict costs no quota.
Unknown skills and domains are reported back instead of being created.

inputs.name: text
inputs.label: Job description
inputs.default: Senior NLP Engineer at Acme. Required: Python, PyTorch, HuggingFace Transformers. Preferred: vector databases. Nice to have: Kubernetes.

features.title: List and view jobs
features.summary: All jobs with skill counts, or one job's requirements ordered by tier and weight.
how: Read-only queries; an unknown id returns 404.

features.title: Delete a job
features.summary: Removes the posting and its requirement edges.
how: DETACH DELETE in one transaction; returns 204, or 404 if missing.

features.title: Deterministic skill-gap analysis + graph payloads
features.summary: Scores how well a user fits a job using only the graph and fixed rules, and returns ready-to-draw data for the skill graph and roadmap flowchart.
how: One read transaction gets each required skill's status (met, partial, missing), shared domains and prerequisite paths up to 3 hops.

Pure rules: a missing skill counts its full weight, a partial one half. Each prerequisite you own cuts the gap by 15% (max 40%). Core, preferred and nice-to-have are weighted 1.0, 0.6 and 0.2. A shared domain adds 2.5% (max 5%).
The response also carries react-force-graph nodes/links and @xyflow/react nodes/edges built from the real Neo4j edges.
Same graph in, same score out; the scoring_version field shows which rules were used.

features.title: Career pivot analysis (Gemini)
features.summary: Gemini describes a target role's typical skills; fixed rules then score how far the user is from it, crediting transferable skills.
how: The graph is read first, so an unknown user fails before any LLM call.
The role profile is cached by role text; role skills are renamed to canonical names before scoring.

features.title: Legacy extract endpoints
features.summary: The original /extract routes, kept for compatibility. They now run through the same cached, strict ingestion pipeline.
how: /extract/resume = resume ingestion; /extract/jd = job ingestion that upserts instead of rejecting a taken id.

inputs.name: text
inputs.label: Job description
inputs.default: Data Engineer. Required: SQL, Apache Spark, Airflow. Nice to have: Kafka.

features.title: Gemini rate limiter and budget
features.summary: Every Gemini call passes a global limiter, so the free tier is never exceeded. When the budget is spent the API answers 429 with Retry-After instead of hanging.
how: Limits: requests per minute, requests per day (resetting at midnight Pacific, like Google's quota), and a cooldown after any Gemini 429.
Explanations stop at 80% of the daily budget so resume and job parsing keep working.
Defaults are 8 per minute and 200 per day, set with GEMINI_RPM and GEMINI_RPD.
The test below shows today's usage; to see a 429, restart the API with GEMINI_RPD=1 and parse twice.

features.title: Neo4j circuit breaker and graph health
features.summary: If Aura Free is paused or unreachable, requests fail fast with a 503 and a 'resume your instance' hint instead of crashing or hanging.
how: Short connection timeouts plus liveness checks on pooled connections.
After 3 connection failures in 60 s the breaker opens: calls fail immediately for 30 s, then one probe decides whether to close it.
Domain errors such as 404 and 409 never trip the breaker.
The health check also reports node and relationship counts against Aura Free limits.

features.title: Graph correctness fixes (G1–G5)
features.summary: Fixed duplicate edges, a domain bonus that matched everything, missing jobs scoring 100%, over-counted prerequisites, and LLM output overwriting shared skill data.
how: Relationships are MERGEd on the node pair, then properties are SET, inside one transaction.
The domain bonus counts only domains both sides point at; prerequisites use count(DISTINCT owned).
Unknown users or jobs return 404; Skill properties come only from the ontology file.
Verified by the offline test suite; run it with: python -m pytest

features.title: Generated, idempotent Neo4j seed
features.summary: cypher/seed.cypher is generated from the ontology file, so the graph and the source of truth can't drift, and it's safe to re-run.
how: Run: python scripts/build_seed.py (or --check to verify it's up to date).
Then run cypher/constraints.cypher and cypher/seed.cypher in the Aura console.
The System page warns when the graph has fewer canonical skills than the ontology.

features.title: Visual frontend
features.summary: React app with Analyze (fit ring, 2D skill graph, roadmap flowchart), Users, Jobs, a 3D ontology explorer, the System dashboard and this Features page.
how: Pages are code-split so three.js loads only on the Ontology page.
LLM text is rendered as safe markdown, with no raw HTML.
A global banner shows quota (429) and outage (503) states.

features.title: Offline test suite
features.summary: About 110 tests that need no database, no API key and no network: golden scores, Cypher contracts, the breaker, the limiter, payloads and Omnigent policies.
how: Run: python -m pytest   (frontend: npm --prefix frontend run lint)
tests/test_dashboard_registry.py fails if an API route is missing from this dashboard.

features.title: Multi-agent guardrail policies
features.summary: Custom Omnigent policies, written and unit-tested but not running yet: a shared daily Gemini budget across agent sessions, a cap on sub-agent dispatches to stop revise loops, and a read-only reviewer.
how: daily_llm_budget counts Gemini calls and tokens per Pacific day in a local ledger shared by all sessions.
dispatch_budget denies the 7th sub-agent run in a session.
deny_tools blocks graph-write tools for the Reviewer.

features.title: Omnigent curriculum workflow (Parser → Reasoner → Reviewer)
features.summary: An orchestrator coordinates a local Parser, a Gemini Reasoner that uses NextNode's graph tools, and a local Reviewer from a different vendor that verifies the curriculum against the graph.
how: Agent configs, startup scripts and the design doc are written.
Blocked on the NextNode MCP server, plus installing Omnigent and Ollama.

features.title: NextNode MCP server
features.summary: Exposes NextNode's graph operations as standard Model Context Protocol tools so any agent or MCP client can use them. The tool contract is specified; the server isn't built yet.
how: See docs/TDD-phase3-omnigent.md §3 for the 7 tools and their security model.

features.title: Public demo page (GitHub Pages)
features.summary: docs/index.html: a no-install pitch dashboard with a client-side agent simulation, career graph, features and changelog, published with GitHub Pages.
how: scripts/build_pages.py writes docs/assets/data.js (ontology, this feature registry, sample scenarios); the page loads it with a plain script tag.
The simulation runs a JavaScript port of the Python scoring rules; parsing is mocked and activities are templated.
Its self-test compares the browser results to values computed by the real Python engine.
tests/test_pages.py fails if the generated data is out of date.

features.title: No-install feature sandbox
features.summary: docs/sandbox.html: a visual explorer (career graph, roadmap flowchart, full ontology) with a sample dataset, plus every feature's tester, in one static page. By default the API runs inside the browser; Live mode calls your backend.
how: First visit seeds a sample dataset (3 candidates, 3 jobs). The explorer draws the analyze response's graph and roadmap_flow payloads with d3, and the full ontology from /ontology/graph.
Sandbox mode: assets/mock-api.js answers the same routes, status codes and response shapes as FastAPI, using the real ontology and the scoring port; data stays in this browser's localStorage.
Differences: text is parsed by a keyword matcher instead of Gemini, pivot uses built-in role templates, and explanations are templated.
Live mode: the API serves the page at http://localhost:8000/demo/sandbox.html, so requests are same-origin.
tests/test_pages.py runs the mock API under Node and checks it against the Python engine and the route list.
